title: Biologics water systems: WFI, pure steam, PW | Aquemi

headline: WFI for biologics that holds endotoxin at every point of use, from the clinical suite to the commercial plant
lead: A biologics plant draws Water for Injection (WFI) in volume for media, buffers and the final rinse of every clean-in-place (CIP) cycle, and pure steam for sterilize-in-place (SIP) and autoclaves. Endotoxin in that water ends up in your process, so we design the loop to hold the USP <85> limit of < 0.25 EU/mL, USP <645> 1.3 µS/cm at 25 °C and 500 ppb total organic carbon (TOC) at the furthest outlet, at peak draw. We size it for your batch schedule, leave room for the next suite, and hand over the factory acceptance test (FAT) report and installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) protocols that Health Canada, the FDA and EU inspectors read.

blocks.h: In a biologics plant, water is a process input, not a utility in the background
body: Cell culture media, chromatography and filtration buffers, CIP rinses and the feed to every pure steam generator all start as WFI or Purified Water (PW). Buffer and media preparation draw large volumes in short windows and then stop, so peak draw, not daily total, sets the storage tank, the pump and the loop.

Endotoxin is a critical quality attribute in almost every biologic drug substance and drug product specification. It is heat stable: sanitization kills the bacteria that shed it, but does not destroy what they have already released. A biofilm in a cooled sub-loop or a point-of-use exchanger can put endotoxin into a full media batch long before a monthly sample shows it. We design those weak spots out and show the evidence at qualification.

We work for biologics developers and contract manufacturers, vaccine makers, and cell and gene therapy facilities in Canada, including university and hospital buildings that make advanced therapy medicinal products (ATMPs) for clinical trials.

body: Source: EMA Guideline on the quality of water for pharmaceutical use (EMA/CHMP/CVMP/QWP/496873/2018), Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5, in effect since 1 February 2021. It replaced the earlier CPMP position statement on water for parenteral vaccines. These are minimums. Most biologics plants use WFI for media and buffers even where the table allows PW, because the endotoxin and bioburden limits on the drug substance leave little margin. Your product file and risk assessment set the grade.

blocks.h: Where endotoxin gets into biologics water, and what we design against
rows: Cooled sub-loops and point-of-use heat exchangers
A hot loop feeds cool outlets for media and buffer prep; water that sits warm in an exchanger grows biofilm
Double tubesheet exchangers, drainable layout, a hot sanitization step after each use or on a fixed schedule, and a sample point downstream of each cooler
Low flow at peak draw
Several large buffer draws at once drop return velocity and starve the far end of the loop
Loop and pump sized to the batch schedule, return flow monitored and alarmed, turbulent flow kept as EU GMP Annex 1 paragraph 6.9 requires
Dead legs and capped tie-ins left for expansion
Stagnant branches hold water at temperatures bacteria tolerate
Every branch to an L/D of 2 or less to ASME BPE, future tie-ins as valved points at the loop, not capped stubs
Ambient PW sections ahead of the generator
Reverse osmosis (RO) and storage at ambient temperature are where most biofilm lives
Hot water or ozone sanitization on a stated schedule, and generator feed limits written into the PW design
Membrane WFI and ultrafiltration
Membranes reduce endotoxin but can be breached by integrity failures or biofilm on the permeate side
Integrity testing, continuous TOC and conductivity, and the control strategy the EMA expects from a non-distillation route
Hoses, transfer panels and sampling
Water picks up endotoxin after the outlet valve, then the sample reads as a loop failure
Sampling procedures that match how production draws water, and investigation records that separate the two

blocks.h: Who reads your water system, and where we answer it
cols: What they read on the water system
rows: Health Canada, GMP inspection of biologic drug establishments

GUI-0001 for all drugs, with Annex 2, GUI-0027 (Manufacture of biologics, current edition 4 July 2024) on top: design, qualification, sanitization, monitoring and trend review of the water and steam that touch the process
Health Canada, Biologic and Radiopharmaceutical Drugs Directorate (BRDD)

BRDD reviews biologic clinical trial and new drug submissions and runs the lot release programme. The facility and utilities description in your submission, water included, has to match what the inspector finds
Health Canada, sterile biologics

GUI-0119, Health Canada's adoption of EU GMP Annex 1 (2022): WFI route (6.10), no dead legs and drainable slopes (6.7), turbulent flow (6.9), vent filters (6.11), sanitization (6.12), continuous TOC and conductivity on WFI (6.15) and pure steam (6.17)
Health Canada, cell, tissue and gene therapies
GUI-0027 leaves ATMPs to a separate guide. Until it is issued, Health Canada points manufacturers to PIC/S GMP Annex 2A. Your regulatory team confirms which applies to your product
FDA, sites shipping biologics to the United States

CBER for vaccines and cell and gene therapies, CDER for most therapeutic proteins and antibodies. 21 CFR Parts 600 to 680 with Part 211, read at the pre-license inspection against the FDA Guide to Inspections of High Purity Water Systems
EU authorities and importers

EU GMP Annex 2 for biologics, Annex 1 for sterile products, Part IV for ATMPs, the EMA water guideline and Annex 15 qualification. Membrane WFI needs notice to the GMP supervisory authority before use

blocks.h: How the systems connect in a biologics plant
blocks.caption: PW feeds the WFI still or membrane WFI skid and the pure steam generator, and in many plants also supplies the initial CIP rinse. Hot WFI circulates above 70 °C (EU GMP Annex 1, 6.10) and serves the CIP final rinse hot. Media and buffer preparation take WFI through cooled sub-loops or point-of-use coolers, each with its own sanitization step. Pure steam goes to autoclaves and to SIP of bioreactors, tanks and transfer lines. Monitoring and controls run across all of it, with audit-trailed records under 21 CFR Part 11 and EU GMP Annex 11.

blocks.h: Phased capacity, from the first clinical batch to licensed production

items.d: Small WFI demand, often met with a membrane WFI skid or a compact still, or with purchased bulk WFI for media while PW and pure steam run on site. We write the expansion into the user requirement specification (URS) now.

items.t: Phase 2: design for the commercial plan
items.d: Tank, loop diameter and pump sized for the commercial batch schedule; space, power and valved tie-in points for a second generation train; headers sized for the next suite.
A second train added beside the first, factory tested, tied in during a planned shutdown under change control. The qualification scope is stated before the first cut.

blocks.h: Decisions to settle before the URS is approved

items.d: We size storage and loop flow from your batch schedule: how many buffer and media preparations overlap, how much they draw and how fast. A tank that runs low during a buffer campaign is a deviation, not an inconvenience.

items.t: Hot loop with cool outlets, or an ambient loop
items.d: Hot WFI suits CIP and holds microbes down continuously, but every cool outlet needs a cooler and a sanitization route. An ozonated ambient loop uses less energy and needs proven ozone removal before each use. We compare both on your demand profile.

Both are pharmacopoeial in USP and Ph. Eur. Distillation has the longer record with inspectors and feeds a hot loop directly. Membrane WFI uses no plant steam for generation and needs a stronger control strategy and, for EU markets, a notice to the supervisory authority.

items.t: How single-use your process really is
items.d: Single-use bioreactors and bags cut CIP and SIP water, but media and buffer make-up, autoclaves and any stainless vessel still need WFI and pure steam. We size from the process you will run.

items.t: Make media and buffers, or buy them
items.d: Purchased liquid media and buffer concentrates move WFI demand off site. Hydrated in-house from powder, the same process puts that demand on your WFI peak. Settle it before generation is sized.

Feed temperature can swing from near freezing in winter to over 20 °C in summer, and some municipal supplies use chloramine. We size membranes at your coldest month and design chloramine removal ahead of the RO.

blocks.h: Questions process, validation and QA leads in biologics ask

items.q: We are a start-up with one clinical product. Is a full WFI system justified?
items.a: Not always. Purchased bulk WFI or a compact membrane WFI skid can carry a clinical programme, with PW and pure steam on site. What matters is that the tank, loop and space you build now can take the commercial train later. We set out both routes with their costs and qualification scope.

items.q: Our facility is single-use. Do we still need WFI and pure steam?
items.a: Usually yes. Media and buffers made in-house need WFI, autoclaves need pure steam, and most single-use plants keep some stainless tanks for buffer preparation that need CIP and SIP. Demand is lower and peakier than in a stainless plant, which often favours smaller generation and more storage.

items.q: How do you control endotoxin at cooled points of use?
items.a: With sanitizable double tubesheet coolers, drainable layout, a hot sanitization step on a schedule we justify from qualification data, and a sample point after each cooler. Endotoxin and microbial samples are taken at every outlet during qualification, in the way production draws water.

items.q: Can a cell therapy or university ATMP facility run on PW or DI water?
items.a: For lab support, glassware washers and autoclave feed, often yes. The EMA guideline sets WFI as the minimum for every step of a cell-based ATMP that is not sterilized afterwards, so water that touches those products is WFI, made on site or bought in. We size each grade to what it supplies.

items.q: Will the qualification we do for clinical supply carry into commercial production?
items.a: Most of it, if the design allowed for growth. Added generation and new points of use go through change control, with a risk assessment that sets the scope: usually IQ and OQ for the new section and a period of increased sampling. We state that scope before the work starts.

items.q: Is membrane WFI acceptable for biologics?
items.a: USP allows WFI by distillation or a purification process shown to be equivalent or superior to it, and Ph. Eur. 0169 has allowed reverse osmosis with other techniques since April 2017. For EU markets, notice goes to the GMP supervisory authority before use, and some corporate standards still require distillation. Confirm with your regulatory team product by product; the WFI by membrane page sets out the control strategy.
